note: Rewritten from the original description of the new species in Roonwal & Maiti's paper on the termites of Indonesia, original in English, published in Treubia vol. 27, part 1 (1966); the scan used here has the running head "M.L. ROONWAL & P.K. MAITI: Termites from Indonesia" on p. 13. The original states explicitly that the alate is unknown; the type material comprises 23 soldiers and several large and small workers, the workers not being described morphologically. The passage following the labrum and anteclypeus (postclypeus, maxillae, labium, legs, measurement table 11) lies outside the scan window and is not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier head capsule (excluding the nasus) is almost pear-shaped, distinctly constricted behind the antennal bases; the back of the head is upturned, forming a conspicuous posterior hump (0.47—0.52 mm); the nasus is short and slender, about half as long as the head capsule, upturned in profile, without a nusal node; the antennae have 14 segments, segment 1 the longest, cylindrical and dark, segment 2 the smallest. The alate is unknown.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head and thorax: the head capsule is reddish brown; the nasus brown, darker in the middle and paler at the tip; the antennae reddish brown, becoming paler towards the tip. The thoracic nota and femora are pale brown, the abdominal tergites yellowish brown; the pilosity is sparse, with a few setae on some of the posterior tergites. Total length (with the nasus) about 4.1—4.8 mm. The head capsule (excluding the nasus) is almost pear-shaped and constricted behind the antennal bases; it is bare apart from a pair of setae on the top of the head; slightly longer than wide (head length without the nasus 1.20—1.26 mm, maximum head width 1.10—1.15 mm); widest posteriorly, the posterior margin narrowly rounded; in profile the back of the head is upturned, with a distinct posterior hump (hump 0.47—0.52 mm); the dorsal outline is strongly concave in the middle. The nasus is nearly cylindrical, short and slender, equal in length to half the head capsule; distinctly upturned in profile, without a nusal node; with several setae in front of the tip; behind the antennal sockets there is a pair of suboval white spots on each side. The frontal gland and its duct are conspicuous. The antennae are very long, with 14 segments, the segments slender, all rather densely hairy and with a few long setae and many short setae, the hairs denser on the distal segments; segment 1 the longest, cylindrical and darker than the others; segment 2 the smallest; segment 3 twice as long as segment 2 or slightly more, and only slightly longer than segment 4; segment 5 about as long as segment 4; segments 6—8 progressively longer, segments 9—14 progressively shorter. The labrum is laminar, wider than long; with several setae in the middle of the tip; its anterior margin nearly straight and transparent; the anterolateral corners rounded. The anteclypeus is white, slightly crescent-shaped and far wider than ... (this section is cut off outside the scan window).
